matrix.attribution: Routing: OSRM / FOSSGIS public demo · © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)
matrix.method: OSRM Table fastest-path road distance (metres) and duration (seconds); asymmetric; no fallback_speed.

warnings: Standard car routing, not verified heavy-vehicle routing.
No truck height, width, weight, axle, hazardous-goods or access restriction guarantees.
Travel times are provider estimates; no live traffic, loading, breaks or customs time.
Snapped road positions are not verified facility gates or legal vehicle access.
Alternatives are offered only when the provider returns them; multi-stop alternatives are disabled.
Public demo service: light local use only; no SLA or production capacity guarantee.
GIS locations are candidate references, not verified customers, gates or legal truck access.
Demands: hypothetical. Capacity is a single integer unit: hypothetical units.
Matrix distances follow fastest OSRM paths, not necessarily shortest-distance paths; no live traffic.
Time windows apply to service start; service completion and depot return must fit the vehicle working limit.
Optional-stop priorities weight a lexicographic service penalty before the selected travel objective.
Operating cost excludes tolls. Fuel/driver costs are added only from supplied values; avoid counting them twice in cost/km.
Empty vehicles are not repositioned between different start/end depots. Vehicle minimization is a weighted count-first objective; balance minimizes total metres + 20 × longest route.
Solver schedules use upward-rounded whole seconds/metres; final road geometry may differ at via-points because of OSRM turn continuity.
Vehicle 1: final via-point route differs by more than 5%/100 m from matrix sum. Scheduling/cost uses the validated matrix; inspect before dispatch.
Vehicle 3: final via-point route differs by more than 5%/100 m from matrix sum. Scheduling/cost uses the validated matrix; inspect before dispatch.
